data.name: Faroe Islands
data.summary: The Faroe Islands tax residents' capital income (interest, dividends and gains on shares and other securities) under a separate capital gains tax law at a flat 35% for individuals; ordinary income pays progressive national tax plus 16%-23% municipal tax. Emigrants are deemed to sell securities worth over DKK 100,000. Inheritance is free of income tax, but an inheritance duty (arvaavgjald) of 1%-12% is paid to the probate court; children pay at most 3%. Gifts from parents to children are tax-free. No wealth tax was found.

regimes.name: Full tax liability
regimes.description: Flat 35% tax on capital income and gains; progressive tax on other income; inheritance duty up to 3% for children.
regimes.eligibility: Full tax liability after more than 180 days within a 12-month period or with a registered permanent address (TAKS).

capital_gains.summary: Løgtingslóg nr. 164/2001 on capital gains covers sales of shares, investment certificates and similar securities, debt claims, and also dividends and interest (§ 1). Individuals and estates pay 35% on the net gain (§ 14(2)). On emigration, securities worth over DKK 100,000 (or below acquisition value) are deemed sold; payment can be deferred against a bank guarantee.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Exit tax: deemed disposal of securities over DKK 100,000 on moving away (TAKS).

sources.title: Logtingslog nr. 164 fra 21.12.2001 um skatting av kapitalvinningi (as amended)

open_questions: Gains on real estate are outside this law; treatment of private real estate gains not researched (left null).
capital_gains.rate_basis: § 14(2) Løgtingslóg um skatting av kapitalvinningi: individuals 35% on the computed gain.

dividends.summary: Dividends are capital income taxed at 35% (Løgtingslóg nr. 164/2001 § 1(5) and § 14); Faroese companies withhold 35%. Foreign tax paid on foreign income can be deducted from the Faroese tax up to the tax on that income (TAKS Uttanlandsinntøka).

sources.title: Logtingslog nr. 164 fra 21.12.2001 um skatting av kapitalvinningi (as amended)

dividends.rate_basis: Flat 35% capital-income rate for individuals; 35% withholding on Faroese dividends.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 35% on dividends (refund to treaty rate: UK 5%/15%, Nordic 0%/15%, Switzerland 0%/15%, India 15%/25%).
dividends.treaty_network: Nordic convention, UK, Switzerland, India and a few others.

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax found: TAKS lists taxes on income, interest, gifts and inheritance, pension tax and capital gains tax, with no tax on wealth.

sources.title: TAKS: Taxation in the Faroe Islands

inheritance.summary: Inheritances are free of income tax, but arvaavgjald (inheritance duty) of 1%-12% is paid to the probate court depending on the heir and the size of the share (TAKS). The 1908 Danish inheritance duty act, in force in the Faroes by Anordning 468/1921, sets for spouse and children: 1% on shares up to DKK 1,000, rising in steps to 3% on shares over DKK 100,000 (§ 2 A), the band rate applying to the whole share. Advance inheritance (forskotsarvur) is subject to the duty; ordinary gifts from parents to children are tax-free.
inheritance.important_exceptions: No duty while the surviving spouse keeps the estate undivided (óskift búgv). Spouse and children under 18 have an exemption under conditions (§ 3).

sources.title: Anordning nr. 468 af 08.11.1921 hvorved lov om arveafgift af 27.05.1908 saettes i kraft paa Faeroerne

open_questions: Later amendments to Anordning 468/1921 not checked; the TAKS summary (1%-12%) matches the original table.
Scope for foreign assets of a Faroese-domiciled deceased and whether a spouse in undivided estate (óskift búgv) defers the duty for children not analysed.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts from parents to children are tax-free (TAKS, Skattalógin § 29); advance inheritance pays arvaavgjald.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Estates administered by the Faroese probate court (skiftirættur).

residency.tax_residency_test: More than 180 days in a 12-month period, or a registered permanent address (TAKS).

routes.name: Danish and Nordic citizens
routes.requirements: Danish and Nordic citizens can settle freely; the Faroes are outside the EU, so other EU citizens need permits.

routes.name: Others
routes.requirements: Work/residence permits under Faroese immigration rules; no investor route found.

sources.title: TAKS: Taxation in the Faroe Islands

corporate.summary: Companies and funds pay 18% on capital gains under Løgtingslóg 164/2001 § 14(2); the general corporate rate is believed to be 18% as well (not verified at source).

sources.title: Logtingslog nr. 164 fra 21.12.2001 um skatting av kapitalvinningi (as amended)

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent of the 4 listings of at least 140 m² in Tórshavn municipality (Tórshavn, Hoyvík, Argir) on Kitt.fo, the Faroese rental portal, on 2026-10-15: a 204 m² 5-room house in Hoyvík (DKK 14,500, 6-month let), a 192 m² 3-bedroom-plus-office flat in Argir (DKK 16,900, let over 3 years), a 150 m² house in central Tórshavn (DKK 15,000) and a 145 m² house in central Tórshavn (DKK 13,000), both lets under 1 year. Kitt.fo showed 48 listings in all on that date; no other listing had 4 or more bedrooms. Some rents include electricity, heating and internet. Very thin sample: the Faroese rental market is small and many lets are arranged privately or through Facebook groups, so treat this as indicative only.

intl_school_annual_fee.description: The Faroe Islands have no international school and no private upper-secondary school was found. The leading upper-secondary option is the public Glasir – Tórshavn College (gymnasium and other youth programmes, about 1,500 students), which charges no tuition: Faroese education is free at all levels. Instruction is in Faroese, so a non-Faroese-speaking child would need language support (Glasir runs Faroese-as-a-second-language courses). Fee 0 per child.

cost_of_living.notes: Rent from a very thin Kitt.fo sample (4 listings of 140 m²+ in Tórshavn municipality). There is no international school; public upper-secondary education at Glasir (in Faroese) is free. Trap Faroe Islands confirms Glasir is Tórshavn's merged upper-secondary college and that instruction is in Faroese (https://trap.fo/en/society-and-business/uddannelse-og-forskning-pa-faeroerne/).

data.us_citizen_notes: No US-Faroes treaty; US citizens remain subject to US federal tax.
open_questions: Not in World Bank/WGI data; no authoritative overrides added.
Real estate gains and municipal property tax not researched.

Cost of living: prime rent rests on only 4 Kitt.fo listings (2026-10-15); a Faroese agency or Hagstova rent figure for large houses would firm it up. Fee set to 0 (free public upper secondary in Faroese); there is no international school.
